name: Wang Zhaojun 王昭君
credit: Kosumi Morihage, 17th century (Edo period) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Wang Zhaojun was a lady of the Han palace who, in 33 BC, was given in marriage to Huhanye, the chanyu of the Xiongnu, as part of a peace settlement between the two powers. She lived the rest of her life on the steppe and became one of the best-known figures in Chinese literature, the subject of countless later poems and plays.

The Yuan shi ("Poem of Resentment") is attributed to her by tradition, as a lament composed on her departure for the Xiongnu lands; the attribution is traditional rather than certain. The text is that of Shen Deqian's anthology Gushi yuan (1719). Her birth year here is an approximation, used only for sorting.

poems.title: 怨詩 (Yuan shi)
poems.author: Wang Zhaojun 王昭君
poems.text:
秋木萋萋，
其葉萎黃。
有鳥處山，
集于苞桑。
養育毛羽，
形容生光。
既得升雲，
上游曲房。
離宮絕曠，
身體摧藏。
志念抑沉，
不得頡頏。
雖得委食，
心有徊惶。
我獨伊何，
來往變常。
翩翩之燕，
遠集西羌。
高山峨峨，
河水泱泱。
父兮母兮，
道里悠長。
嗚呼哀哉，
憂心惻傷。
